To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of metal particles in the monomer solution accelerates the polymerisation process, which results in the local gelation near the metal surface.
the addition of 0.5% of tungsten to the ceramic suspension causes an increase in polymerisation reaction rate constant and the activation energy of the reaction decreases by 224 kJ/mol.
tungsten catalyses polymerisation of glycerol monacrylate and this effect should be taken into consideration when designing gelcasting formulations of ceramic-metal composites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of tungsten on the kinetics of the polymerisation process in gelcasting of Al2.
the development of gelcasting method for the preparation of Al2O2–W ceramic-metal composites.
the influence of tungsten filler on gelation process and its influence on polymer structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metal filler has a catalytic influence on the polymerisation of monomer, which results in local polymerisation near the surface of metal particles.

the tungsten filler in alumina suspension catalyses polymerisation reaction and the polymerisation process is faster in the vicinity of metal particles than in the bulk of the suspension, resulting in polymer inhomogeneity and the formation of polymer structure with defects, which is responsible for the lower mechanical properties of the green bodies.
the tungsten particles have a strong impact on the polymerisation reaction and gelation of the ceramic suspension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tungsten has a catalytic effect on the polymerisation of glycerol monomer, which is a key process in gelcasting.
tungsten particles have a significant influence on the polymerisation reaction rate of glycerol monacrylate and the activation energy of this reaction.
the presence of metal particles in alumina suspension has an influence on the polymerisation process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

broadband dielectric spectroscopic measurements can be used for the determination of activation energy of the polymerisation in gelation of ceramic-metal composites, and the results are comparable with rheological measurements.
the broadband dielectric spectroscopic measurements can be used for the determination of activation energy of gelation in the gelcasting process.
the dielectric spectroscopy can be used as an effective tool to study polymerisation in gel casting of ceramic-metal composites.
